::: {.hero}
# MNIST Generative Models Lab

<p class="hero-pitch">
I built this as a hands-on curriculum from scratch classifiers through CNN comparison to VAE, DDPM, DCGAN, and latent diffusion, not a single benchmark script.
</p>

<div class="hero-actions">
<a class="btn btn-primary-cta" href="chapters/01-why.html">Read the case study</a>
<a class="btn btn-secondary-cta" href="https://github.com/jt-09/mnist-generative-models-lab">View GitHub repo</a>
<a class="btn btn-secondary-cta" href="assets/ext/report.pdf">Open technical report</a>
</div>

<p class="hero-summary">
Built an end-to-end MNIST ML lab from scratch KNN, logistic regression, and MLP through CNN classification (99%+ accuracy) to generative models including VAE, DDPM, DCGAN, and latent diffusion, documented as an interactive Jupyter learning path with a reflective technical report.
</p>
:::

## What this project demonstrates

::: {.landing-section}
- From-scratch ML implementation
- PyTorch CNN training and evaluation
- Model comparison and error analysis
- Generative modeling tradeoffs
- Technical writing and reproducibility
:::

## Skills demonstrated

::: {.landing-section}
- NumPy implementation of KNN, softmax regression, and MLP training loops
- PyTorch model training, evaluation, and visualization
- CNN architecture design and confusion analysis
- Generative modeling with VAE, DDPM, DCGAN, and latent diffusion
- Experiment documentation, artifact hygiene, and reproducibility
:::

## Learning path

I followed a fixed order: understand the data, implement classical models by hand, add a CNN, benchmark everything side by side, then explore four generative families.

::: {.fig-wide}
![Learning path from EDA through manual classifiers, CNN comparison, and generative models](assets/ext/figures/00_roadmap/learning_path.png){fig-alt="Flowchart of the project learning path: EDA, KNN, logistic regression, MLP, CNN, model comparison, VAE, DDPM, DCGAN, and latent diffusion."}
:::

<p class="fig-followup">
The left half of the path is classification. The right half is generation. I kept saved notebook outputs so you can read metrics and plots without retraining.
</p>
